newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metro downbeat despite H1 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Metro downbeat despite H1 profit rise.

text.p: Newly-merged German retail group Metro AG published its first half-year results on Thursday showing a gain in operating profits, but sales were flat and the company gave a downbeat business outlook.
Group operating profits rose to 181 million marks ($119.4 million) from 48 million marks, but turnover was a touch lower at 29.1 billion marks against 29.2 billion marks in the same period of 1995.
The company predicted a full-year operating profit of between 1.0 and 1.1 billion marks, based on the assumption that pre-Christmas business performs in line with last year.

Metro shares have barely moved since their first listing in July after the group fused with ASKO Deutsche Kaufhaus AG, Deutsche SB-Kauf AG and Kaufhof Holding AG. The company did not offer much hope for investors.
"The consumer climate...did not significantly improve in July and August or in the first weeks of September," the company said in a statement.
"Uncertainty about Germany's economic future as a place to do business in general and job fears affected consumer attitudes."

Germany's economy is suffering from near-record post-war unemployment of over 10 percent but is starting to emerge from a winter trough. Metro said it doubted economic forecasters who predict a revival in the all-important Christmas season.
Metro recently revised down its 1996 full-year sales forecast by three billion marks to 62 billion marks.
"Metro AG for the meantime does not expect any improvement in the consumer climate in 1997," the statement continued.
A breakdown of first-half operating profit figures showed that Metro's wholesale operations contributed 125 million marks and building stores earned 94 million marks.
But losses in department stores of 95 million marks and of 68 million marks in furniture shops, plus extra costs for the holding company reduced the profit gains.
The company invested 620 million marks in the first half, and expanded sales area by 1.9 percent to 7.3 million square metres. Full-time staff were reduced by 4.1 percent to 130,495.
Shares in Swiss-controlled Metro opened up 2.50 marks at 138.50 marks, but were still slightly below their debut price of just over 140 marks in July.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.515 German Marks)
